opening_sentence: These results measure recovery of simulator-defined faults and do not demonstrate production outage-prediction accuracy.

spec_basis.spec: UptimeTrace M3.0 simulator v2 and ground-truth specification v4.5.1

differences_from_spec.D1: ABRUPT/SILENT incidents are never 'detected'; spec stage 2 is a labelled diagnostic only (approved)
differences_from_spec.D2: alerts before ABRUPT/SILENT-only windows are strict false alarms for the budget (spec: unattributed, excluded from N_FA); spec-style rate reported separately (approved, A5)
differences_from_spec.D3: PRECURSOR incidents with no evaluable decision count as missed (currently 0)
differences_from_spec.D4: Brier/calibration, detection delay, lead-conditional recall are new
differences_from_spec.D5: candidate set = quantile grid + explicit no-alert and all-alert boundaries, fixed tie-breaks (spec leaves open)
differences_from_spec.D6: operational-target training view is the separately reported secondary experiment E2 (spec lists it as required); never in headline or model selection
differences_from_spec.D7: ABRUPT/SILENT chance baseline mandatory in the first evaluation, strictly diagnostic

task.target: a merged incident begins in (t, t + horizon]
task.evaluation_unit: merged incident (primary fault decides the group)

data.model_settings: existing fixed settings of ml/train_baselines.py; any change is an amendment

test_ood: reported as ood_slow and ood_cache_node subgroups and pooled

E2_operational_target.rule_not_repeated: scores do not depend on the training view

split_usage.negative_thinning: only on train, only for memory, recorded; never on val or test

precedence: excluded_active (oracle active-incident mask: onset <= t < oracle_mask_end)
decision_point_status.O(t): all merged incidents with onset in (t, t+H], no exclusion filter
decision_point_status.excluded_points: no score, no alert, no exposure, no label, never counted as negatives
decision_point_status.unscorable_points: evaluable: can alert, count as exposure, masked only from the row-level primary label view
decision_point_status.exposure: evaluable decision points x 60 s, decision-quantised; dedup-suppressed intervals stay in exposure

alert_emission.rule: scan evaluable decisions in time order; alert iff score >= threshold and (no previous alert or t >= previous_alert_time + 900 s)
alert_emission.suppressed_crossings: counted and reported; not alerts, no credit, not false alarms
alert_emission.score_assertion: scores must be finite float64 in [0,1]; NaN or out-of-range aborts the run (makes the two boundary thresholds exact)

matching.stage_1: PRECURSOR incidents by increasing onset take the earliest unconsumed alert in the credit window; one alert credits at most one incident
matching.stage_2_for_ABRUPT_SILENT: diagnostic only; never feeds recall, precision or the budget

duplicate.definition: not a hit; inside the credit window of a PRECURSOR incident already credited to another alert

late.definition: not hit/duplicate; a PRECURSOR onset lies in (t, t+H] but less than 120 s ahead

coincident_unpredictable.definition: O(t) non-empty and contains only ABRUPT/SILENT incidents

alert_outcomes.assertion: an unconsumed alert inside a PRECURSOR credit window must belong to an already-detected incident
alert_outcomes.never: an alert is never credited because an ABRUPT or SILENT incident follows

incident_outcomes.PRECURSOR: detected iff stage-1 matched; otherwise missed (including unevaluable)
headline_must_include: predicted share of all incidents = K/N

metrics.pooling: ratios of sums over runs of the split/subgroup
metrics.precision_lenient: (hits + duplicates + late) / alerts; 'N/A (zero alerts)' when alerts == 0
metrics.false_alarm_label: conditional on the oracle active-incident mask and the data-sufficiency exclusion; not a deployed false-alarm rate

detection_delay.definition: alert_time - precursor_start of the primary fault (oracle quantity), detected PRECURSOR only

brier.primary_view: evaluable rows, unscorable masked, y = positive
brier.calibrators: raw score (primary) and val-fitted isotonic (secondary); alerts always use the raw score

reliability_bins.source: validation scores only (sorted raw scores of all evaluable validation decisions), per frozen model entry (rule once; logreg and xgboost per training seed and experiment)
reliability_bins.duplicates: discard every boundary equal to the smallest validation score S[0] (it would create an empty first bin); then unique remaining boundaries ascending e_1 < ... < e_m; bins (-inf,e_1), [e_i,e_{i+1}), [e_m,+inf); tied levels merge, never split; no bin is empty on validation; if every boundary is discarded there is a single bin (-inf,+inf), reported
reliability_bins.actual_bin_count: m + 1 (at most 9), reported per model/seed together with the collapsed or discarded levels
reliability_bins.empty_bin_on_test: reported with n = 0 and no estimate; boundaries never re-derived from test
reliability_bins.isotonic: same raw-score bins; mean predicted = mean calibrated value

metrics.pr_auc_row_level: diagnostic only, prevalence shown, never in a headline

abrupt_silent_diagnostic.label: diagnostic: not prediction success
abrupt_silent_diagnostic.observed: proportion of incidents of the group with at least one emitted alert in [o-1800 s, o-120 s]
abrupt_silent_diagnostic.shift: per run offset d_r uniform on {1..20159} decision steps (20160 per run); move each emitted alert j -> (j + d_r) mod 20160; drop alerts landing on an excluded decision; apply the circular dedup; recompute pooled proportion
abrupt_silent_diagnostic.seed: numpy.random.default_rng([20261202, training_seed]) for logreg/xgboost; array shape (1000, n_runs); runs in sorted run-id order; one fixed draw per training seed; the deterministic rule uses default_rng([20261202, 0])

algorithm: 0 or 1 alerts: keep (gap into a single alert is N)
gap into alert a = forward distance from the previous alert in circular order (last precedes first)
cut the circle at every gap >= 15 into maximal chains whose internal gaps are all < 15; a chain starts at an alert whose incoming gap is >= 15
inside each chain: keep the first alert; keep a later alert iff its forward distance from the last kept alert is >= 15 (exactly 15 keeps)

properties.example: alerts at 20155 and 2 are 7 apart: 20155 kept, 2 dropped (a linear scan from 0 would keep 2)

circular_dedup.precondition: input alerts come from section 4 so consecutive alerts are >= 15 apart on the line; only the (last, first) pair can be closer on the circle; at least one gap >= 15 always exists; evaluator aborts if two or more alerts have no gap >= 15

metrics.model_comparison: paired run-level bootstrap of differences; 'better' needs a 95% interval excluding 0 on Recall_P and neither model's test verdict equal to 'budget exceeded' or 'budget exceeded with confidence'

zero_alert_rule.applies_when: a model emits no alerts in the evaluated set
zero_alert_rule.seed_mean: over seeds with defined precision only; print 'defined in n of 5 seeds' (rule: 'defined' or 'N/A')

bootstrap.handling: excluded from the precision percentile interval; number excluded reported

threshold_selection.objective: maximise validation Recall_P among feasible candidates (FA_strict <= B)
threshold_selection.reason: dedup makes the relation non-monotone; no bisection
per: frozen model entry (rule once; logreg and xgboost per training seed and experiment)
threshold_selection.primary_model_type: from E1 validation results only: highest mean-over-seeds validation Recall_P at budget; ties rule < logreg < xgboost; if every E1 model's mean validation Recall_P is 0 no primary model is named; E2 never enters; named before the freeze

quantile_candidates.threshold: S[min(n-1, ceil((1 - m_k) * n))] ('higher' quantile) over the sorted evaluable validation scores S, n = len(S)

all_alert_boundary.effect: every evaluable decision meets score >= 0.0; alerts limited only by the 900 s dedup

no_alert_boundary.effect: strictly above the maximum possible score; zero alerts, FA_strict = 0, Recall_P = 0

candidate_set.deduplication: exact float64 equality; sorted ascending; at most 2002 unique candidates; list length and SHA-256 recorded
candidate_set.evaluation: every candidate, boundaries included, through the identical emission, dedup, matching and strict false-alarm pipeline on all 30 validation runs

fields.boundary_selected: exactly one of no_alert | all_alert | lowest_quantile | highest_quantile | none (precedence rule)
fields.seeds_selecting_no_alert_per_model: count for logreg and xgboost; rule shown as '1 evaluation: yes/no'

no_alert_and_boundary_reporting.treatment_on_test: evaluated as a never-alerting system (Recall_P = 0, zero alerts); calibration and Brier still computed; never dropped or hidden

definitions.lowest_quantile: theta* == smallest quantile-derived candidate (theta_0, tail mass 0.1)
definitions.highest_quantile: theta* == largest quantile-derived candidate (theta_1999, tail mass 1e-5)

boundary_label_precedence.co_occurrence: all_alert may equal lowest_quantile (90th-percentile score 0.0); all quantile candidates coincide for a constant scorer; no_alert never co-occurs (exceeds 1.0)
boundary_label_precedence.informational_field: boundary_labels_also_matching (lower-precedence labels that also equal theta*; never used in a decision)

candidate_set_hash.serialisation: concatenation of each candidate's 8-byte little-endian IEEE-754 float64, ascending deduplicated order

uncertainty.seed_reporting: per-seed and mean with min/max over logreg and xgboost seeds only; best seed never selected; rule evaluated once with no seed statistics

order: train logreg and xgboost with each of the five seeds for E1 and E2; rule has no training and is evaluated once, in E1 only

select thresholds on val for every model/seed/experiment (candidate set incl. boundaries); derive reliability-bin boundaries from validation scores; fit isotonic calibrators on val; name primary model type from E1 validation only

freeze: write frozen_run.json (hashes of protocol, manifests, requirements.lock, git commit, model artifacts; 21 model entries (rule once with training_seed null + 5 seeds each of logreg and xgboost for E1 and for E2) each with exact threshold (repr and hex), candidate-set hash and length, single-valued boundary_selected with boundary_labels_also_matching, no_alert_selected, reliability-bin boundaries and actual bin count, isotonic calibrator, validation metrics; chance-diagnostic seed; training seeds; primary model type or 'none'; time of freezing; own SHA-256)
evaluate test_iid and test_ood (and subgroups) once, E1 and E2, including the chance diagnostic
freeze_and_isolation.poison_file_test: replace test files with files that raise on read and run train/select pipeline to completion
freeze_and_isolation.post_hoc: anything changed after test numbers were seen is marked post-hoc and excluded from headlines
freeze_and_isolation.amendments: protocol version bump and full re-run; results from different versions are not compared

sections: frozen-run summary (incl. no_alert_selected / boundary_selected flags and actual reliability bin counts)
E1 headline table (strict false-alarm rate with spec-style rate in its own column)
secondary experiment E2 (own section, never in headline)
headline_columns: strict false alarms per evaluable host-day

limitations.ood_coverage_weak: 10 of 20 OOD runs are statistically identical to train; other 10 only 2.5x slower ramps
limitations.rows_autocorrelated: about 30 near-identical positive rows per incident

unresolved_ambiguities: detection delay uses the latent precursor_start (oracle, not observable)
decision-grid resolution (60 s) limits sub-minute alert timing
numerical choices changeable before the freeze: bootstrap B=10000 and seed 20261201, chance-diagnostic seed 20261202, training seeds 101-105, interior reliability quantile levels
heavily tied scorers (e.g. rule) give fewer reliability bins because tied boundaries merge
the spec extract preserves only sections 13-16; the sections they cite remain only in the scratchpad source
the deterministic rule uses chance-diagnostic stream id 0, so its shifts differ from the seeded models' shifts (descriptive comparisons only)

review.result: approved in principle; final-review amendments B1-B6 applied
review.freeze: not frozen; explicit approval required before freezing or training

previous.result: approved in principle with amendments A1-A6
previous.freeze: not frozen; explicit approval required before freezing or training

amendments_log.A1: threshold candidates = 2000 quantile candidates + no-alert boundary nextafter(1.0, +inf) + all-alert boundary 0.0, deduplicated, all evaluated; no-alert selection reported; infeasible outcome replaced; scores asserted in [0,1]
amendments_log.A2: reliability-bin boundaries derived from validation scores only, frozen before test, shared by IID/OOD/subgroups, ties merged deterministically (boundaries equal to the minimum validation score discarded so no bin is empty), actual bin count reported
amendments_log.A3: operational-target view is secondary experiment E2, separately reported, never used for primary-model selection
amendments_log.A4: 1000 seeded circular-shift ABRUPT/SILENT baseline mandatory in first evaluation, strictly diagnostic
amendments_log.A5: strict false-alarm definition kept; spec-style rate reported separately
amendments_log.A6: no validation safety margin; mechanical generalisation verdicts
amendments_log.B1: budget verdict is one ordered mutually exclusive rule: lower 95% bound > 1 -> 'budget exceeded with confidence'; else point estimate > 1 -> 'budget exceeded'; else 'budget reproduced'
amendments_log.B2: rule is deterministic: evaluated once, E1 only; five training seeds apply only to logreg and xgboost; 21 frozen entries; rule uses chance-diagnostic stream id 0; no seed statistics for rule
amendments_log.B3: precision is 'N/A (zero alerts)' for a model with no alerts; alerts and Recall_P stay 0; probability metrics still computed; defined aggregation and bootstrap handling
amendments_log.B4: circular-shift dedup defined on the circle: cut at every gap >= 15 steps into chains, greedy inside each chain; rotation-equivariant; same 900 s interval and exclusion handling
amendments_log.B5: boundary_selected single-valued by precedence no_alert > all_alert > lowest_quantile > highest_quantile > none; exact threshold (repr, hex) and candidate-set hash preserved
amendments_log.B6: sections 13-16 of simulator spec v4.5.1 copied verbatim from the exact source with provenance and hashes

E2.rule_not_repeated: scores do not depend on the training view

table: strict false alarms per evaluable host-day with 95% interval
spec-style false alarms per evaluable host-day

ordered_first_match_wins.if: lower 95% bound of the test strict false-alarm rate > 1

verdict_rule.lower_bound_definition: lower end of the 95% run-level bootstrap percentile interval of the strict false-alarm rate per evaluable host-day
verdict_rule.equality: a lower bound exactly equal to 1 does not trigger the first rule; a point estimate exactly equal to 1 is 'budget reproduced'
verdict_rule.note: a lower bound > 1 implies a point estimate > 1

resolved_by_review: no-alert models evaluated on test as never-alerting systems (confirmed)

never: artificial rule seed variability in summaries
deterministic_rule_baseline.reliability_bins: derived once from the rule's validation scores
deterministic_rule_baseline.chance_diagnostic_stream: numpy.random.default_rng([20261202, 0]); id 0 reserved for deterministic models, not a training seed; rule-versus-model comparisons in this diagnostic are descriptive
deterministic_rule_baseline.summaries: seed mean/min/max/SD over logreg and xgboost seeds only; rule shown as one row 'deterministic, 1 evaluation' with run-level bootstrap interval only; no_alert tally shown as '1 evaluation: yes/no'
deterministic_rule_baseline.primary_model_selection: the rule's single validation Recall_P is compared with the seed means of logreg and xgboost; tie order unchanged
